elements.problem: Plain Hemoptysis has no amount, so the rule fires on any blood coughed up. That is over-inclusive: a patient with blood-stained sputum recorded as Hemoptysis would be made Urgent, although the page sends small amounts to the 'exclude TB' branch. SNOMED has no 'massive hemoptysis' concept. This is the closest fit, but the threshold is lost.
evidence: Urgent: HIV danger signs before starting ART :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hemoptysis" "finding"))

elements.problem: Agitation is encoded as 'Feeling agitated', which is the patient's own feeling. 'Psychomotor agitation' (finding) is the closer concept for agitation the clinician observes. Minor concept choice.

Urgent: HIV danger signs before starting ART :: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Feeling agitated" "finding"))

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Feeling agitated' is a subjective feeling. Psychomotor agitation is the closer concept for an observed danger sign.

summary: The red box is encoded fully and correctly as one Urgent rule anchored on HIV. The only loss is the haemoptysis volume threshold (>= 1 tablespoon), which makes the rule over-inclusive. The flowchart's TB-symptom screen (possible TB, gated on no known TB) and the meningitis -> urgent branch are correct. Jaundice and pneumonia/PJP from the 'other acute illness' decision are not encoded at all. The CD4/CrAg branches are lab-gated and not representable.
